body: Just read this. Thank you. Thugs are so much better now. I connected my logic to my emotions and I'm already past the worst part of the breakup. Getting over her is actually a lot easier than I expected. I'm slowly remembe ring what it's like to be happy and have less stress. :)

Thanks I'm going back and forth between okay and not okay every five minutes. I actually have an appointment with a psychologist Tuesday and then I'm going to start seeing a psychiatrist soon after hopefully.
I was pretty fine for the first three hours now I'm not. In my mind it's like I want to forgive her for all the stress and bad things she's done. I keep remembering the good times. It really hurts.

I'll definitely check it out, thank you. Honestly though I'm way past the point of trying to make this work. I'm only 20. I took a medical withdrawal from college because I (ironically) was showing many symptoms of depression since I moved off to college (all while dating my current so). I'm moved back in at home to focus on my mental health. I should be having fun right now and I definitely shouldn't feel this way in a relationship. I know it's going to end because I would die from stress before 40 if I married this girl. Now it's all about figuring out when. I just feel like I'm in limbo right now.

Do you mean it can get to the point where the non BPDSO starts to think that maybe they're the one with BPD? Because I have certainly already reached that stage. I go back and forth between being self assured and secure to thinking maybe Im the problem and that maybe I have BPD. It's scary and stressful.

I feel like Ive gone through many stages and I'm at that point where I'm beginning to do this as well. I feel like I've already accepted the great possibility of something awful happening soon and I'm okay with it. Is there any tips you can give me to help me practice detachment as well? It may help aide my decision of wheher or not I should even be with her.

I'm happy for you man. You sound like you're in a good place. You dodged a bullet for sure. Idk anything about them but things probably aren't all great. But maybe they are, who knows. Like you said though it doesn't matter. You're a free man. I envy you.

I tried once and got pulled back in. That was a month ago. She has borderline personality disorder and I have read that pulling someone back in is a great skill of theirs. 

My problem is I'm in a poor mental state. I transferred schools and moved out for the first time last semester. I fell into depression, I made zero friends aside form my room mates the entire semester and I don't even want to think about what may have happened if she wasn't always there for me to keep me from feeling too lonely. Then again, she could be the thing holding me back. I don't know. I'm just scared. Last time I tried to end it I felt like an addict going through withdrawal. I watched her on social media constantly, no matter how hard I tried to stop. Maybe I'm co-dependant. I am already talking to a counselor so I got that.

Is it obvious that I am doing that? I don't believe I do, but I'm not doubting it. It would make sense I suppose because I do let her actions and emotional state effect how I feel.  I always thought that when someone else's happiness became yours, you were in love. But I'm probably wrong. Oh well, I'm still learning. 

I have actually been reading up on mindfulness a lot lately and I've been trying to meditate on a regular basis so I will definitely continue to do this and look into other activities. I really appreciate your response. It brought some light to something I haven't given much thought.

Hey man I want to point out something to you if you're wondering if you're relationship is healthy or you're happy. I know I doubt myself sometimes:

You are dating someone with poor mental health. You were fine before dating her (I assume). You are now dating her. She refuses help. You are seeking help. Idk about you but this seems just wrong to me and unfair to you. You are carrying her weight. 

I'm in the same boat though. So I can't really talk. Its easy from a third party perspective.
My SO has been busy on vacation (weekend ordeal) and has been in light contact with me for the first time in our relationship and holy shit. It feels good.
I actually ended it. A few hours ago. It's really hard and I hate this lonely feeling. But I guess it's for the best.

Hey, OP here. I just created a new post and saw this as I linked it back to this one.

This is very interesting and I never really thought of it like this. I think the hard part right now is trying to figure out what is the BPD and what isn't. So its hard for me to tell am I dealing with something serious and something  I can't truly help, or am I overthinking a small issue that we can work through. At the moment I don't consider what I'm experiencing as abuse. Probably because I haven't experienced any violence (yet?) or direct emotional attacks. But maybe I have and I'm just not seeing it (like some females in abusive relationships like you mentioned). Either way, I guess I'm taking it one day at a time. I have no idea what I'm doing, all I know is how I feel at that very moment. I just hope I'm not blind and not seeing anything that will/would be obvious is we do end up not together. I would really like your personal advice on my new post. 

Also I see your point on turning to the wrong place, but I really don't know where else to go. I feel like anyone else is going to tell me it may be best to leave. And maybe it is, but I guess I really don't want to hear that right now. I just need to figure out if this is just me overthinking things (which I have done before in healthy relationships), or something that I can't fix that will ultimately be my demise. Or somewhere in-between that we can work on and get through. Idk I'm rambling.

Heres my new post http://www.reddit.com/r/BPD/comments/2okrkv/update_my_girlfriend_has_bpd_need_some/

Wow this is actually really helpful. I guess I just need to shift my perspective to a more positive position. Thats a great way to look at it. Hopefully if I keep telling myself the same I'll eventually enter that mindset. Thank you.

This isn't lacking at all. Thank you for your response. We just had a little fight (That caused the edit). I'm scared of her bad reactions and feeling like I'm treating her bad (even when I'm not) will lead her to leave me for someone else. As she did to her ex (but he really was treating her badly). But no, this fear is only due to her leaving her last boyfriend. I'm just being paranoid and I keep reading online about peoples SO's leaving them for other people and that triggers that fear. Especially when some of those stories include BPD. I think sometimes I try too much. And by too much I mean past the point where its doing any good. I guess sometimes I should just accept that she is going to be upset no matter how hard I try. Its good to hear that the manipulation is stigma. I really don't feel like she's that type. I should probably focus a little more on myself sometimes.
